rationale: Clinical and molecular characterization of KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621390 / NEDSFBA) demonstrates a clinical presentation centered on mild-to-severe intellectual disability, epilepsy/febrile seizures, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle facial dysmorphic features (such as trigonocephaly or mild dysmorphisms). Cohort delineation (Sleyp et al., 2022; Kuroda et al., 2024) confirms the absence of obligate congenital heart disease, prominent neurovisceral storage signs, focal limb-reduction defects, or rapidly lethal early neurodegenerative progression. The presence of these major structural or storage manifestations strongly argues against isolated KLHL20-related disease and suggests alternative syndromic, metabolic, or chromosomal etiologies.

evidence.text: Characterization of 14 individuals with de novo missense variants in KLHL20 established a recurrent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features, without gross structural visceral/cardiac malformations or neurodegenerative storage features.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features.

evidence.text: A patient with a novel de novo KLHL20 variant presented with early-onset West syndrome, developmental delay, and mild dysmorphic features including trigonocephaly, expanding the phenotypic seizure spectrum without neurovisceral storage or limb reductions.

source.title: Early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay associated with a novel KLHL20 variant
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Her dysmorphic features included trigonocephaly, prominent... intellectual disability, and epilepsy... As such, KLHL20related neurodevelopmental disorders may expand.

new_directions.question_text: What specific facial biometric measurements or stereophotogrammetric patterns distinguish KLHL20-related facial dysmorphism from other monogenic epilepsy/autism syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Facial dysmorphism in KLHL20 patients is reported as subtle. Deep phenotyping and 3D facial imaging could establish quantitative phenotypic signatures to assist in targeted clinical identification prior to exome sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-Kelch domain loss-of-function variants in KLHL20 produce an overlapping or distinct, potentially more severe phenotype compared to Kelch-propeller missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Currently described human variants cluster in the substrate-binding Kelch-type beta-propeller domain. Establishing whether haploinsufficiency or truncated alleles cause lethality or non-neurological structural anomalies would delineate the full gene-disease spectrum.
